tagline: Oaks and magnolias line three miles through Penney’s farming experiment.
intro: Much of the J.C. Penney Memorial Scenic Highway runs beneath oaks and magnolias, with most of the canopy dating to the early 1900s. This three-mile stretch of SR 16 received its Florida scenic-highway designation on April 30, 2010. Florida Scenic Highways highlights the corridor’s history, culture and natural resources, including the Penney Retirement and New Hope communities.

J. C. Penney founded Penney Farms in 1922 as an experimental farming village. A real estate decline and the stock market crash reduced his ambitions to a community for retired Christian ministers. New Hope traces its history to 1923, when African American sharecropper families lived there during Penney’s crop experiments.

Traveling east from the Starke side, SR 16 passes through Penney Farms before continuing toward Green Cove Springs. The retirement community’s historic district borders SR 16, Caroline Boulevard, Wilbanks Avenue and Studio Road. Along the scenic corridor, the landscape includes bottomland hardwoods, commercial forest, mesic hammock and wetlands.

moments.title: Penney Farms
moments.text: Penney Farms began as a planned farming village, briefly called Long Branch City. Florida incorporated the town in 1927. Within its boundaries, New Hope preserves another part of that agricultural history: the community dates to Penney’s 1923 crop experiments and housed African American sharecropper families. Faith and worship remain part of New Hope’s community life.

moments.title: Penney Retirement Community
moments.text: The retirement community carries the earlier name Memorial Home in its historic-district designation. Designated in 1999, the district contains 24 historic buildings and two structures. Its French Norman architecture is one of the corridor’s cultural resources. Penney’s reduced farming venture became a home for retired Christian ministers; the 192-acre community now includes Christian laypeople, clergy and missionaries. SR 16 forms one boundary of the district; Caroline Boulevard, Wilbanks Avenue and Studio Road define the others.

moments.title: Oak and magnolia canopy
moments.text: Oaks and magnolias form a canopy over much of the three-mile corridor. Most of that canopy dates to the early 1900s. The byway also passes through bottomland hardwoods, commercial forest, mesic hammock and wetlands.
moments.notice: Look for the oak and magnolia canopy over the corridor.
